okay, so where i live there are two very prominent big butterflies. the yellow and black tiger swallowtails, which are easy to catch, and the perceptive dark brown or black ones with the white or cream band across their wings. sorry, i don't know what that kind is called, but it's the big one. they're perceptive and quick to escape. there are of course a bazillion other butterflies, but these two are the most visible.

so in elementary school, i could catch the coffee and cream ones if i was real lucky. then i'd make a tent with my hands and scare the crap out of dumb girls on the playground, until i'd open my hands and let the butterfly loose, while the girls would feel really dumb for being afraid of such a regular bug.

around the same age, at a lake campsite, i found a black triangle chillaxing on a grill set one cold morning. upon closer inspection, it was guess what. so i got it to crawl onto my finger and took it into the cabin, where i used the black triangle to scare the everloving crap out of a middle aged lady. then the black triangle began to vibrate much to her horror and shock, and when it opened its wings to reveal a brilliant brown spread, she looked incredibly dumb and ashamed as the butterfly took off.

related stories involving bugs and scaring people

at the lake with the cabin, i caught a remarkably big hoverfly in the windowsill. when gripped properly, it would pretend to sting me. obviously, being a fly, it had no stinger, but it was kind of neat that it would at least pretend. apparently some people thought it was in fact stinging me and i was not reacting. i've also seen hoverflies with yellow rear 4 legs and thick black front legs, and they'd wave their black front legs around as if they were antennae.

"pincher beetles', also known as longhorned spruce bark beetles, or spruce beetles. they can come in a surprising variety. around here, we have the black ones with the white speckles. they make "eek eek" noises when you touch them, until they run out of air. they're very good at scaring people. in elementary school, i saw a trio of kids crushing a bug and acting like it was a lego-sized terrorist. i just so happened to have a scary pincher beetle on my thumb, so i came up and said "are you being mean to my friend???". they ran away screaming.

clearwing bee hawkmoths are also bizarrely frightening to some people, as are their hornworms that love to eat fireweed and attempt to cross the road every four summers. on a side side note, we also have had real honest to god hummingbird sightings in my arctic area. hummingbirds. with beaks and bird legs and feathers and internal heating system. someone must have brought them here.
